title: Shared social profile stats across four networks: durable paid runs, verified aliases and subscription quota admission
steps: S1: the domain chain for a network runs its providers in order; a technical failure moves on, not_found stops at once, a non-profile URL fails before any call.
S2: two accounts ask /social-stats for the same page; a provider's daily cap is spent; a refresh fails after a good snapshot.
S3: the tab merges the door's answer into the rows and asks only for pages nothing is known about; the button of one row sends at most four pages.
S4: a site-check row a worker still holds is asked again; a worker whose lease ran out writes its result late.
S5: RapidAPI fails; the Facebook Apify attempt starts, loses its lease or response, resumes after restart/day rollover, and is read by a second account. Validate piloted rows and source identity.
S6: Instagram/TikTok run and dataset resume across workers; verified alias force/reassignment/negative handle; RapidAPI billing-cycle and YouTube Pacific-day admission.
expect: S1: the first working provider answers with no fallbackFrom; not_found ends the chain; the non-profile URL never reaches a provider.
S2: one row serves both accounts; a spent cap defers the row to the next UTC day without using an attempt or the paid fallback; the failed refresh keeps the old numbers and retries after an hour.
S3: numbers reach the row by its page URL in the views' vocabulary and the row is re-scored; a missing number stays absent, never 0; the poll never asks forever for a page the server left out.
S4: the held row keeps its lease and attempts; the late write is rejected and the newer worker's row stays intact.

S5: one paid run and ledger reservation serve both accounts; resume preserves age and run id; unknown POST never starts again even on force; cap0/provider/account/money refusal starts nothing; invalid or empty data preserves the stale snapshot; followers/dates come from observed rows and coverage stays partial.

S6: pinned mapper preserves null/partial; alias+snapshot publish is fenced; force aliases share a generation; explicit ID never changes owner; pending results converge without another provider call; vanished handle does not tombstone its ID; cycle/PT quota refuses the whole chain before any call.
evidence: Listing survey with real calls, tasks/evidence-wo-social-stats/listing-survey.md (19/10/2026): FB 100/month, TikTok 100/month, Looter 150/month, Stable 20/month, yt-api 300/month free; the council's four P0 points in tasks/todo-wo-social-stats.md (queue re-queued held rows and wrote results without an owner check; stats stored as days not timestamps; no budget per billable call)
fence: chain.mjs advances only on technical codes; social-stats.js reserves a budget unit per provider and per account before every call and defers on refusal; durable-queue.js enqueues conditionally and fences every write with the lease token; mergeSocialStats keeps shown numbers on queued or failed refreshes; social-apify.js checkpoints before POST, records late immutable run receipts, resumes by run id, and validates held money/day before start; facebook-apify.mjs validates observed identity and dates without inventing complete coverage; shared service commits permanent deployment/UUID admission and the existing queue atomically, with authority and observed generation fences; replica identity/binding/state versions stay independent; client outbox retains UUID and cannot call providers or bypass unreconciled legacy work
